sourceGeneration.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Make a controlled synthetic photographic contact sheet. One wide image consists of exactly three equally sized square, strictly top-down orthographic, separate photographs arranged edge-to-edge in a single row, with only a straight seam at one-third and two-thirds. No text or markings. All three use the same white matte work surface, soft minimal shadows, and camera magnification. Show only flat-laid examples of the SAME dark charcoal steel hex-head M8 bolt and the SAME dark charcoal steel hex nut. All pieces are fully visible, sharp and physically identical across photos. The bolt takes about 32% of a panel in length, the nut about 12% of the panel in diameter. On every bolt make the hex head distinctly wide and the threaded shaft distinctly narrow so its two ends are easy to tell apart from above. Nuts are compact hexagonal objects with a clear round through-hole, viewed flat from overhead.
LEFT PANEL, first example: one horizontal bolt, broad head on the left and narrow free tip pointing right. One nut lies just to the right of that tip on the bolt's long centerline, with a visible narrow white gap. Pair centered in panel.
MIDDLE PANEL, second example: one vertical bolt, broad head at top and narrow free tip pointing DOWN. One nut lies immediately below that tip on the same vertical centerline, with a narrow white gap. Pose and gap are the first example rotated 90 degrees and shifted a little to the right.
RIGHT PANEL, whole inspection scene, exactly two bolts and two nuts. Both bolts lie horizontally, with the broad head on the RIGHT and narrow free tip pointing LEFT. The correct pair is in the lower left, around two-thirds of the height: one nut lies just left of the tip of the lower bolt, aligned on its centerline with a narrow white gap, like a 180-degree rotation of the first example. The other bolt is in the upper right. The other nut is below the CENTER of that upper-right bolt, a clear distance sideways from that bolt's horizontal axis, NOT in front of its left tip. Give all four items large white separations, unambiguous outlines, and realistic but matte metal texture. The test must contain exactly the same two kinds of hardware, repeated twice, with no extra hardware, no boxes, no labels, no crop marks, no hands, no background clutter.

sceneGeneration.prompt: Transform the attached square placement guide into ONE physically realistic overhead photograph of identical, dark, matte steel M8 bolts and identical dark hex nuts on a plain nearly white tabletop. Preserve the guide geometry, empty margins, scale, orientations, square framing, and the exact center of EVERY object. There are exactly 3 short bolts and exactly 6 loose nuts. The top-left bolt points right, top-right bolt points down, bottom-left bolt points left. Match each guide silhouette: broad distinctive hex head and narrow threaded shaft, with the actual head on the end indicated by the guide. Each group has a nut ahead of the tip and another nut sideways, on perpendicular rays. Preserve precisely the equal center-to-center radii within each group. DO NOT reposition or enlarge any object; accurate centers and clearly separated white gaps matter most. Keep placement of the rightmost nut near the edge, fully visible, and leave the lower-right quadrant blank. Realistic detailed machining texture, round apertures in all 6 nuts, crisp boundaries, very faint soft shadows. Strictly overhead orthographic view. No extra parts, arrows, numbers, text, grid marks or labels.
